_comment: Regression seeds: failure patterns the eval has caught and that must not silently re-enter the codebase. Each entry references a case_id that already lives in golden.json (so the case is exercised by the standard eval run). run_evals.load_cases() reads this file at runtime and emits a warning if any seeded case_id has been removed from golden.json — that's the drift guard. To add a new regression seed: add the entry here AND ensure the corresponding case is present in golden.json with full annotation.

seeds.added_in_iteration: Option B — multi_part_complaint rule for draft-response
seeds.description: Multi-part complaint where the responder honestly hedges some sub-issues but makes an assertive fix-like claim about another sub-issue at low overall confidence (< 0.4). The judge ruled this misleading_fix_claim. The multi_part_complaint rule added to draft-response targets exactly this pattern.

seeds.added_in_iteration: Option B — multi_part_complaint rule for draft-response
seeds.description: Same multi-part pattern as civ7_gameplay_002. The judge's ruling on this case has been borderline across recent runs (sometimes honest_hedge, sometimes misleading_fix_claim). Locked here so future regressions on the same pattern are caught.
seeds.judge_ruling_before_fix: borderline (honest_hedge or misleading_fix_claim depending on prompt revision)

seeds.added_in_iteration: Iteration 1 — action_severity_precedence rules for draft-response + critique-draft
seeds.description: Two-rung downward action swap (escalate → monitor) on a review explicitly using hard-blocker language ('unplayable', 'crashing constantly', 'pervasive'). Pre-fix the responder defaulted DOWN the action ladder under low patch confidence. Rule 1 (severity-overrides-confidence) targets exactly this — hard-blocker language must produce escalate regardless of patch evidence confidence.

seeds.added_in_iteration: Iteration 1 — action_severity_precedence rules for draft-response + critique-draft
seeds.description: One-rung upward action swap (no_action → monitor) on a pure DLC-pricing opinion ('half the game locked behind dlcs'). Pre-fix the responder treated subjective monetization feedback as trackable. Rule 2 (subjectivity-caps-the-ladder) targets exactly this — pure pricing/design opinion defaults to no_action and the existence of related patches does not raise the rung.

seeds.added_in_iteration: Iteration 1 — action_severity_precedence rules for draft-response + critique-draft
seeds.description: Negative-direction guard for Rule 1. This case mentions hard-blocker language ('pretty much unplayable') but its ideal action is monitor, not escalate — the complaint is a multiplayer-server lag pattern, not a hard-blocker crash. Locked to catch future drift where Rule 1 over-fires on the bare presence of hard-blocker words. The case must STAY at proposed_action == 'monitor'; promotion to escalate is the regression this seed guards.
